meta.instrument: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 - as amended upto March 12, 2025
meta.authored: Read from the held text, clause by clause. NOT generated from master sheet.xlsx. Hand-authored against reference/ and every rule carries the words it came from in `quote`.
meta.scope: Schedule A and Schedule B ONLY - the two that bind a LISTED COMPANY. Checked against the headings rather than assumed: Schedule A is '[See sub-regulation (1) of regulation 8] Principles of Fair Disclosure'; Schedule B is '[See sub-regulation (1) of regulation 9] Minimum Standards for Code of Conduct FOR LISTED COMPANIES'. Schedule C is the same code 'for Intermediaries and Fiduciaries', Schedule B1 the one for Mutual Funds under Reg 5F, and Schedules D and E are the informant's own forms. None of those is this product's user.
meta.why: SS4a left these as the last unread part of PIT. The generated corpus carries 11 rules citing Schedule A or B, covering A.1 to A.5 and B.3, B.4, B.4(2) and the contra-trade restriction. Schedule A has 8 clauses and Schedule B has 15. The 14 here are the ones nothing carried.
readingNotes: SCHEDULE B1 sits INSIDE what looks like Schedule B, and it is the MUTUAL FUND code of conduct under Reg 5F of Chapter IIA. Its clauses restart at 1 and read almost identically to Schedule B's - compliance officer reporting, trading window, pre-clearance - against a different duty-holder. Reading Schedule B to the next SCHEDULE heading swallows it whole, which is SS3t's Schedule III trap: the text contains clauses that are real, current, and about somebody else.

Schedule B's clause NUMBERING IS STABLE across the 2018 and 2019 amendments. Clause 7 reads '7. [***]' - the content omitted and the slot kept - so a clause number means today what it meant then. That is what makes a wrong clause citation a real error rather than a version difference.
Clause 7 is omitted and carries no obligation. It is not in this file.

miscitation.PIT-SCHEDULE-B-CL-3-28: The generated corpus carries a rule titled 'Pre-clearance' citing 'Schedule B cl. 3'. Clause 3 of Schedule B is designated persons and their immediate relatives being governed by an internal code; PRE-CLEARANCE IS CLAUSE 6. The substance of that rule is right and its citation is wrong, so a Company Secretary who followed it to verify against the regulation would read clause 3 and find nothing about pre-clearance. pit_master.json is generated from the owner's spreadsheet and must not be hand-edited (SS2k), so PIT-SCH-B-6 here carries the correctly cited version and quotes it.

rules.title: Ensure information shared with analysts and research personnel is not unpublished price sensitive information
rules.detail: The code of practices and procedures for fair disclosure must ensure that information shared with analysts and research personnel is not unpublished price sensitive information.
rules.quote: Ensuring that information shared with analysts and research personnel is not unpublished price sensitive information
rules.frequency: On every analyst or research interaction
rules.evidence: The fair disclosure code clause; the pre-read or deck cleared before each analyst meeting; attendance record
rules.notes: The duty bites BEFORE the meeting, not after: once UPSI has been said in an analyst call the only remedy left is Schedule A cl. 4, prompt dissemination to make it generally available. This is the clause that decides whether an earnings call becomes a selective disclosure.

rules.title: Put transcripts or records of analyst and investor meetings on the official website
rules.detail: Develop best practices to make transcripts or records of the proceedings of meetings with analysts and other investor relations conferences available on the official website, to ensure official confirmation and documentation of the disclosures made.
rules.quote: Developing best practices to make transcripts or records of proceedings of meetings with analysts and other investor relations conferences on the official website to ensure official confirmation and documentation of disclosures made
rules.frequency: On every analyst or investor conference
rules.evidence: The transcripts or recordings as published, with their dates; the website location
rules.notes: This is the clause that makes an analyst call auditable. Note LODR Reg 46(2) separately requires audio or video recordings and transcripts of analyst calls on the website within stated periods - this schedule states the principle, LODR states the deadline, and a company can satisfy one and breach the other.

rules.title: Handle all unpublished price sensitive information on a need-to-know basis
rules.detail: All unpublished price sensitive information is to be handled on a need-to-know basis.
rules.quote: Handling of all unpublished price sensitive information on a need-to-know basis
rules.evidence: The fair disclosure code; the structured digital database showing who the information reached and why
rules.notes: The same principle appears in Schedule B cl. 2 for the code of conduct and in Reg 3(1) as a prohibition. Three places, one duty - and the structured digital database under Reg 3(5) is what evidences it.

rules.title: The compliance officer must report to the board, and to the Audit Committee chairman, at least once a year
rules.detail: The compliance officer reports to the board of directors and in particular provides reports to the Chairman of the Audit Committee, if any, or to the Chairman of the board of directors, at such frequency as the board of directors stipulates, but not less than once in a year.
rules.quote: The compliance officer shall report to the board of directors and in particular, shall provide reports to the Chairman of the Audit Committee, if any, or to the Chairman of the board of directors at such frequency as may be stipulated by the board of directors, but not less than once in a year
rules.timelineText: At such frequency as the board stipulates, but not less than once in a year

due.cadence: Not less than once in a year

rules.evidence: The compliance officer's report with its date; board or Audit Committee minutes recording that it was placed
rules.submitTo: Board of directors; Chairman of the Audit Committee
rules.notes: Once a year is a FLOOR, not the requirement - the board may stipulate more often and then that is the duty. Like Reg 9A(4) this files nothing anywhere, so the minute is the only evidence it happened. Note the report goes to the Chairman of the Audit Committee specifically, not to the committee at large.

rules.title: Carry Chinese Walls procedures in the code, and a process for crossing the wall
rules.detail: All information is handled within the organisation on a need-to-know basis, and no unpublished price sensitive information is communicated to any person except in furtherance of legitimate purposes, performance of duties or discharge of legal obligations. The code of conduct must contain norms for appropriate Chinese Walls procedures, and processes for permitting any designated person to cross the wall.
rules.quote: All information shall be handled within the organisation on a need-to-know basis and no unpublished price sensitive information shall be communicated to any person except in furtherance of legitimate purposes, performance of duties or discharge of legal obligations. The code of conduct shall contain norms for appropriate Chinese Walls procedures, and processes for permitting any designated person to “cross the wall”
rules.evidence: The code clause setting out the Chinese Walls norms and the wall-crossing process; records of each wall crossing
rules.notes: Two requirements about the CONTENT of the code, and the second is the one most codes omit: a process for permitting a designated person to cross the wall. A code with a Chinese Walls clause and no crossing procedure does not satisfy this, and the crossing is what the structured digital database under Reg 3(5) then has to record.

rules.title: Do not reopen the trading window earlier than forty-eight hours after the information becomes generally available
rules.detail: The timing for re-opening of the trading window is determined by the compliance officer, taking into account various factors including the unpublished price sensitive information in question becoming generally available and being capable of assimilation by the market, and in any event not earlier than forty-eight hours after the information becomes generally available.
rules.quote: The timing for re-opening of the trading window shall be determined by the compliance officer taking into account various factors including the unpublished price sensitive information in question becoming generally available and being capable of assimilation by the market, which in any event shall not be earlier than forty-eight hours after the information becomes generally available
rules.frequency: On every reopening of the trading window
rules.timelineText: Not earlier than forty-eight hours after the information becomes generally available

due.when: The unpublished price sensitive information becomes generally available

rules.evidence: The compliance officer's record of the reopening decision, with the time the information became generally available
rules.notes: Forty-eight hours is a FLOOR and not the answer: the clause requires the compliance officer to consider whether the market has been able to assimilate the information, so the right date can be later. The PIT Control Centre computes the earliest permitted reopening from this clause and the results meeting in the meetings register - it shows the floor, not a decision.

rules.title: Require pre-clearance by the compliance officer for trades above the threshold the board stipulates
rules.detail: When the trading window is open, trading by designated persons is subject to pre-clearance by the compliance officer if the value of the proposed trades is above such thresholds as the board of directors may stipulate.
rules.quote: When the trading window is open, trading by designated persons shall be subject to pre- clearance by the compliance officer, if the value of the proposed trades is above such thresholds as the board of directors may stipulate
rules.frequency: On every trade above the threshold

due.when: A designated person proposes a trade above the threshold

rules.evidence: The board resolution setting the threshold; the pre-clearance applications and approvals register
rules.notes: This is CLAUSE 6. The generated corpus carries a rule titled 'Pre-clearance' citing Schedule B cl. 3, and clause 3 is designated persons and their immediate relatives being governed by an internal code - so following that citation to the regulation finds nothing about pre-clearance. Clause numbering in this Schedule is stable: clause 7 reads '7. [***]', the content omitted and the slot kept. Note also that the THRESHOLD is the board's to set, so a code with no stipulated threshold has not implemented this clause.

rules.title: Take a declaration that the applicant holds no unpublished price sensitive information before approving a trade
rules.detail: Prior to approving any trades the compliance officer is entitled to seek declarations that the applicant for pre-clearance is not in possession of any unpublished price sensitive information, and must have regard to whether any such declaration is reasonably capable of being rendered inaccurate.
rules.quote: Prior to approving any trades, the compliance officer shall be entitled to seek declarations to the effect that the applicant for pre-clearance is not in possession of any unpublished price sensitive information. He shall also have regard to whether any such declaration is reasonably capable of being rendered inaccurate
rules.evidence: The signed declaration filed with each pre-clearance application
rules.notes: The second sentence is the one that carries the work: the compliance officer must consider whether the declaration is CAPABLE OF BEING RENDERED INACCURATE - that is, whether UPSI is expected to arise before the trade settles. Collecting the declaration and filing it does not discharge that.

rules.title: Fix a window of not more than seven trading days for executing a pre-cleared trade
rules.detail: The code of conduct must specify a reasonable timeframe, which in any event is not more than seven trading days, within which trades that have been pre-cleared have to be executed by the designated person, failing which fresh pre-clearance is needed for the trades to be executed.
rules.quote: The code of conduct shall specify any reasonable timeframe, which in any event shall not be more than seven trading days, within which trades that have been pre-cleared have to be executed by the designated person, failing which fresh pre-clearance would be needed for the trades to be executed
rules.timelineText: Not more than seven trading days from pre-clearance
rules.evidence: The code clause stating the timeframe; the pre-clearance register showing approval and execution dates
rules.notes: Seven trading days is a CEILING on what the code may allow, not the period itself - the code must state its own timeframe and may state a shorter one, and then that shorter one binds. Not computed here: they are TRADING days, there is no exchange trading calendar in this app, and the clock starts at a pre-clearance this app does not record.

rules.title: Stipulate the formats for pre-clearance, trade reporting, decisions not to trade, and holdings
rules.detail: The code of conduct must stipulate such formats as the board of directors deems necessary for making applications for pre-clearance, reporting of trades executed, reporting of decisions not to trade after securing pre-clearance, and for reporting the level of holdings in securities at such intervals as may be determined as being necessary to monitor compliance with these regulations.
rules.quote: The code of conduct shall stipulate such formats as the board of directors deems necessary for making applications for pre-clearance, reporting of trades executed, reporting of decisions not to trade after securing pre-clearance and for reporting level of holdings in securities at such intervals as may be determined as being necessary to monitor compliance with these regulations
rules.evidence: The four formats as annexed to the code, board-approved
rules.notes: FOUR formats, and the third is the one most codes lack: reporting a DECISION NOT TO TRADE after pre-clearance was obtained. A code that provides for applying and for reporting executed trades, but not for reporting that an approved trade was abandoned, has not implemented this clause.

rules.title: Stipulate the sanctions and disciplinary actions the company may impose, including wage freeze and recovery
rules.detail: Without prejudice to the power of the Board under the Act, the code of conduct must stipulate the sanctions and disciplinary actions, including wage freeze, suspension and recovery, that may be imposed by the listed company required to formulate a code of conduct under Reg 9(1) for the contravention of the code.
rules.quote: Without prejudice to the power of the Board under the Act, the code of conduct shall stipulate the sanctions and disciplinary actions, including wage freeze, suspension, recovery, etc., that may be imposed
rules.evidence: The sanctions clause of the board-approved code; the record of any action taken under it
rules.notes: The named sanctions are a minimum the code must provide for - wage freeze, suspension and recovery - and 'without prejudice to the power of the Board' means the company's own action does not displace SEBI's. A code that says only that violations will be 'dealt with appropriately' does not stipulate anything.

rules.title: Promptly inform the stock exchanges of a violation of these regulations
rules.detail: The code of conduct must specify that where the listed company required to formulate a code under Reg 9(1) observes that there has been a violation of these regulations, it shall promptly inform the stock exchanges where the concerned securities are traded, in such form and manner as the Board specifies from time to time.
rules.quote: The code of conduct shall specify that in case it is observed by the listed company required to formulate a code of conduct under sub-regulation (1) of regulation 9, that there has been a violation of these regulations, it shall promptly inform the stock exchange(s) where the concerned securities are traded, in such form and such manner as may be specified by the Board from time to time

due.when: The company observes a violation of these regulations

rules.evidence: The intimation to each exchange with its filing timestamp; the internal record of the observation and the inquiry
rules.notes: The 2019 substitution changed who is told: the earlier wording required the company to inform THE BOARD (SEBI), and it now requires the STOCK EXCHANGES. A code carrying the old wording directs the intimation to the wrong regulator. Distinct from Reg 9A(5), which requires SEBI to be informed of a LEAK of unpublished price sensitive information - a company can owe both at once, to two different recipients.

rules.title: Collect names and PAN of relatives and material financial relationships from designated persons annually and on change
rules.detail: Designated persons must disclose to the company, on an annual basis and as and when the information changes, the names and Permanent Account Number or other identifier authorised by law of their immediate relatives, of persons with whom they share a material financial relationship, and the phone and mobile numbers used by them. The names of the educational institutions from which designated persons graduated and the names of their past employers are also disclosed, on a one-time basis.
rules.quote: Designated persons shall be required to disclose names and Permanent Account Number or any other identifier authorized by law of the following persons to the company on an annual basis and as and when the information changes
rules.timelineText: On an annual basis and as and when the information changes
rules.evidence: The annual declarations from every designated person, with PAN; the record of interim changes; the one-time education and past-employer disclosures
rules.notes: TWO triggers, and the second is what fails: annually AND as and when the information changes. An annual collection alone leaves the register wrong for up to a year. Note the material financial relationship limb reaches beyond family, and the education and past-employer names are a ONE-TIME disclosure rather than an annual one - three different cadences in one clause.

rules.title: Have a process for how and when people are brought inside on a sensitive transaction
rules.detail: Listed entities must have a process for how and when people are brought inside on sensitive transactions. Individuals should be made aware of the duties and responsibilities attached to the receipt of inside information, and of the liability that attaches to misuse or unwarranted use of such information.
rules.quote: Listed entities shall have a process for how and when people are brought ‘inside’ on sensitive transactions. Individuals should be made aware of the duties and responsibilities attached to the receipt of Inside Information, and the liability that attaches to misuse or unwarranted use of such information
rules.evidence: The documented wall-crossing process; the notice given to each person brought inside, with its date and their acknowledgement
rules.notes: Two limbs: the process, and making the individual AWARE of the duties and the liability. The second is what turns a name in the structured digital database into an informed insider, and it is the limb a database alone does not evidence. Inserted by the 2025 amendment, so a code written before March 2025 will not carry it.
